skill.name: lifi
skill.description: Integrate LI.FI APIs for cross-chain swaps, bridges, Composer deposits, Earn discovery, portfolio tracking, and intent-based orders. Covers quotes, transaction preparation, status recovery, supported assets, fees, and implementation patterns.
skill.summary: Build LI.FI integrations for cross-chain routing, DeFi execution, yield discovery, intent orders, and transaction status recovery.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, API documentation, and placeholder credentials. Confirmed static findings are expected outbound calls to LI.FI services. Semantic review found high-impact transaction and arbitrary contract-call guidance that needs stronger confirmation and validation controls.

remediation.issue: Wallet approvals and transactions can move user assets without an explicit final confirmation requirement.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before every approval or signature. Display chain, tokens, amount, recipient, spender, fees, slippage, minimum output, and decoded call details.

remediation.issue: The contractCalls workflow accepts manual destination calldata without defined trust checks.
remediation.suggestion: Treat contractCalls as advanced and opt-in. Decode and simulate calldata, validate chain and target contracts, reject unknown selectors, and require separate confirmation.

remediation.issue: Examples place an API key placeholder directly in request headers.
remediation.suggestion: Show server-side secret loading from an environment variable or secret manager. Keep the existing warning against client-side key exposure.

high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented contractCalls endpoint supports arbitrary destination contract calls with manual calldata. The surrounding guidance recommends Composer but does not define validation or confirmation controls.

content.value_statement: Cross-chain swaps and DeFi workflows require many APIs, transaction checks, and recovery paths. This skill guides LI.FI integration for quotes, execution, tracking, yield, and intents.
actual_capabilities: Explains LI.FI quote, route, transaction preparation, and status endpoints.
Guides cross-chain bridges and same-chain token swaps.
Covers Composer deposits and withdrawals for supported tokenized DeFi positions.
Describes Earn vault discovery, APY and TVL fields, and portfolio positions.
Documents intent quote, order submission, status, and funding models.
Provides Python, JavaScript, and curl integration examples with retry guidance.
limitations: The skill does not hold private keys, sign transactions, or broadcast wallet operations.
Quotes, routes, APY, TVL, protocol support, and service availability can change quickly.
Composer supports selected tokenized positions and may produce partial cross-chain outcomes.
Remote API responses and transaction payloads require independent validation before signing.

use_cases.title: Add Cross-Chain Swaps
use_cases.description: Design quote, approval, execution, and status flows for a wallet or decentralized application.

use_cases.title: Automate Treasury Routing
use_cases.description: Compare routes, fees, timing, and recovery options before moving assets between supported chains.

use_cases.title: Research DeFi Yield
use_cases.description: Filter Earn vaults, compare normalized metrics, and plan Composer deposits with clear risk checks.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Cross-Chain Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a LI.FI route from [source token] on [source chain] to [destination token] on [destination chain] for [amount]. Summarize output, duration, fees, approval needs, and risks. Do not sign or send a transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Design Status Tracking
prompt_templates.prompt: Design LI.FI status polling for [application]. Include backoff, terminal states, timeouts, partial completion, refunds, and user messages. Preserve transaction hashes for recovery.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Composer Deposit
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Composer deposit from [source asset and chain] into [vault]. Verify vault eligibility, approval address, slippage, minimum output, partial outcomes, and confirmation requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Architect a Production Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Architect a production LI.FI backend for [product]. Cover authentication, caching, route selection, transaction validation, explicit confirmations, retries, observability, privacy, and recovery. Separate read-only discovery from asset-moving operations.

output_examples.input: Compare a USDC transfer between two supported chains and explain the safest next step.
output: Route summary: estimated output, duration, network fees, bridge, and minimum received.
Approval summary: token, spender from the current quote, exact amount, and required confirmation.
Next step: verify all displayed details, refresh stale quotes, then request an explicit signature.

output_examples.input: Find suitable USDC vaults and explain how a Composer deposit would work.
output_examples.output: A concise vault shortlist with APY, TVL, lock, KYC, transaction support, and freshness notes, followed by a confirmation-first deposit plan.

output_examples.input: Explain a transaction status that completed with a different destination token.
output_examples.output: The result is partial, not lost. The response should identify the received token, estimate recovery costs, and avoid recovery when gas is disproportionate.

best_practices: Refresh quotes after approvals and before signing because transaction data can become stale.
Use the approval address returned by the current quote and prefer exact token allowances.
Require explicit confirmation for every asset-moving action and preserve transaction hashes for recovery.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode approval spenders, transaction payloads, or assumed bridge routes.
Do not expose API keys in browser code, logs, prompts, or marketplace content.
Do not treat timeouts, missing status records, or partial completion as automatic fund loss.

faq.question: Does this skill custody funds or private keys?
faq.answer: No. It provides integration guidance and request patterns. Wallet software or application code performs approvals, signatures, and transaction broadcasts.

faq.question: Is a LI.FI API key required?
faq.answer: The core API can work without a key at lower limits. Earn requires a key, which should remain on a trusted server.

faq.question: Can it support same-chain swaps?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the same source and destination chain in a quote, then validate and execute the returned transaction through a wallet.

faq.question: Can it execute transactions automatically?
faq.answer: The guidance covers transaction preparation, but every approval and signature should require explicit user confirmation and independent validation.

faq.question: Does vault ranking provide financial advice?
faq.answer: No. APY and TVL are changing data points, not guarantees. Users must assess protocol, contract, liquidity, lock, and market risks.

faq.question: How should partial completion be handled?
faq.answer: Identify the received destination token, compare recovery swap costs with its value, and explain the options before requesting another transaction.
